newsitem.title: USA: CALIF. UTILITIES EYE SLIGHT RELIEF FROM HEAT WAVE.
newsitem.headline: CALIF. UTILITIES EYE SLIGHT RELIEF FROM HEAT WAVE.

text.p: California electric utilities expected to see some relief from the record energy demand on their systems this week, as the heat wave over the state showed signs of easing Thursday.
"We're looking at slightly lower demand after yesterday's record high," said Cory Warren, a spokesman for Pacific Gas & Electric Co (PG&E), a subsidiary of PG&E Corp.
On Wednesday, PG&E reached a peak demand record at 21,484 megawatts (MW), up slightly from the one set a year ago.
Warren said the San Francisco-based utility did not expect Thursday's peak demand to surpass 21,000 MW.
But inland central California cities like Fresno and Sacramento were predicted to see temperatures well above 100 degrees F, he noted.
PG&E, the state's largest electric utility, serves about 13 million people in northern and central California.
"We're looking at lower demand on our system," said Steve Conroy, spokesman at Southern California Edison Co (SoCal Edison), a subsidiary of Edison International.
The central California coastal communities served by SoCal Edison were predicted to see temperatures in the high 80s to low 90s F today, about 10 degrees below Wednesday.
Yesterday, SoCal Edison, based in Rosemead, Calif., posted a record peak demand at 19,084 megawatts (MW), up more than 300 MW from the previous peak set Tuesday.
SoCal Edison provides electricity to about 11 million people within central, coastal and southern California.
Although air-conditioning demand was projected to dip and there was sufficient supply to meet the high usage, SoCal Edison asked customers to use energy "wisely."
